concepts.def: Activities transforming inputs into outputs of goods or services; aim to maximise efficiency and quality.
Output per worker or per hour; UK output per hour was 16% below the G7 average in 2023 (ONS).
Actual output / maximum output x 100; high utilisation lowers unit fixed costs but risks bottlenecks.
Toyota (1948 onwards): minimise waste in time, materials, defects; just-in-time stock and kaizen improvement.
Inventory arrives only as needed; reduces holding costs but requires reliable suppliers; vulnerable to disruption (COVID, Suez 2021).
Japanese for continuous improvement; small ongoing changes from all employees, central to lean philosophy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Operations Management — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Operations Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Operations Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

numericals.q: If actual output is 800 and maximum is 1000, what is capacity utilisation (%)?

free_texts.q: Which Japanese car company developed lean production?
